body.x: A fall in a care home, or a pressure sore that develops over several nights in bed, is the kind of event staff want to catch early. In senior care facilities, those minutes decide how quickly someone can respond.

AITRON Inc., a startup based at Yeungnam University in Gyeongsan, North Gyeongsang Province, builds AI and smart sensor technology for that setting. Founded in 2022, the company says its CEO, Hojun Lee, studied at the New York Institute of Technology (NYIT) and that it set up an overseas entity in Vietnam in 2026. AITRON will exhibit at FIX 2026 through the 15th Daegu International Robot Industry Expo (ROBEX 2026), with product marketing as its stated purpose.

At the exhibition, AITRON plans to introduce what it calls a Wellness-based Smart Care Solution, designed for retirement communities and nursing facilities. The company says the solution combines three parts. An AI-powered edge device for motion recognition detects fall risks in real time and analyzes daily activity patterns. A high-precision smart motion sensor mat analyzes a senior's sleep, which AITRON says helps prevent bedsores and improves sleep quality. A beacon-based SOS system covers emergencies. Together, the company says, they form a closer safety network than any one of them alone.

AITRON says the edge AI device is proprietary technology and describes the response time it secures as a "Golden Hour" in care facilities. It also reports that it has verified the effectiveness of its smart care solution scientifically: it ran clinical trials approved by an institutional review board (IRB) and published the results in a journal indexed in the Science Citation Index (SCI).

The company lists several milestones. It was selected for the Eureka Park section of CES in 2023 and 2024, two years in a row, and took part in MWC Barcelona in 2025, where it says it formed practical partnerships with global partners. In 2026 it was selected for the DGIST Deep-tech Startup Hub Program, run by the Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST), and it is currently conducting a proof of concept (PoC).

Looking ahead, AITRON says it will connect its solutions with care robots it is co-developing with global partners. The company states its ultimate goal as an intelligent healthcare service that lightens caregivers' workloads and raises seniors' quality of life.

On exports, the application names China as its current market and the United States as the market it wants to enter. It cites certification and logistics management as its difficulties, and its plan is to establish a U.S. entity.

FIX 2026 is a future-industry exhibition, now in its third year, that links innovative technologies from four sectors: future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. It will be held from Wednesday, Oct. 21, to Saturday, Oct. 24, at EXCO in Daegu. The theme is "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," and the program includes AI-based technology exhibitions, conferences and lectures by Korean and international experts, and networking sessions that share industry trends and core technologies.
